name: GA-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Jasmine Clark's large fundraising and outside-spending edge
Prediction markets price near-certain Democratic win
Open seat removes incumbency factor but not structural lean
model.rationale: The district's +21 Democratic lean, Clark's roughly $1.6 million raised against a Republican with no reported fundraising, and markets pricing a Democratic win at 97% all point to a safe Democratic hold. No polls or expert ratings exist, so uncertainty stays moderately wide.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a surge in Republican outside spending would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 13th District is a heavily Democratic Atlanta-area seat, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward Democrats. David Scott's retirement set off a competitive Democratic primary, and state Representative Jasmine Clark emerged as the nominee after Everton Blair won only the unexpired-term nomination. Clark enters the general election with a strong financial position, having raised about $1.6 million and benefited from more than $4 million in outside support, while Republican Jonathan Chavez reports no fundraising on file.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals and market pricing, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold. The open seat adds some uncertainty, but the structural lean is difficult to overcome.
